title: Ministers can’t control gas prices, but they can attack other energy costs more ruthlessly
summary: Louise Haigh talked the right talk at the CBI this week, but greater ambition and tighter timelines are needed Shocked by average annual energy bills at £2,166 for the first three months of next year? Here’s worse news. It is currently possible, and perhaps even likely, that the regulator, Ofgem, will set the price cap at £2,000-plus in every quarter of 2027. Predictions for bills are less certain the further out one looks, it should be said. Gas prices, the overwhelming culprit in the £443 hike in the cap announced on Wednesday, can always fall – and might do so if calm returns to the strait of Hormuz. Continue reading...

title: The Guardian view on rising energy prices: only bold action can win public confidence | Editorial
summary: Andy Burnham needs a radical vision of economic change to move on from policies aimed at giving voters ‘breathing space’ Ask Andy Burnham a question and it won’t be long before he mentions the cost of living. Responding to the results of midterm elections in the US earlier this month, he said that the Democratic party’s triumph meant that there was “an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all, and that’s the cost of living”. This wasn’t a non sequitur. The Republicans lost control of Congress in large part because Donald Trump failed to address concerns about the cost of basic goods – a failing aggravated by the US president’s disastrous war against Iran, which caused a spike in commodity prices, exacerbating the affordability problem. title: How datacentres are driving an illegal mining rush in the Amazon ‘more devastating than gold’
summary: As demand for tin ores pushes up prices, criminal gangs are exploiting Indigenous lands and weak regulation to profit from Brazil’s abundant cassiterite While searching for documents tied to an illegal cassiterite export network last September, Brazilian federal police officers were surprised to find a link between an illegal mining and money-laundering scheme and an address connected to one of Brazil ’s biggest showbusiness stars from the 90s. Alexandre Pires, a popular pagode singer-songwriter, is now under investigation as part of Operation Disco de Ouro (Gold Disc) for his alleged involvement in a scheme to illegally ship cassiterite worth millions of dollars abroad. During the investigation, police uncovered a message in which his agent, Matheus Possebon, allegedly admitted to his participation and said that he failed to deliver the illegal ore he had promised his associates. title: Energy bills jump: how to switch providers and is it worth it?
summary: It is possible to switch to a better tariff and save money despite the 26% price rise in January Average energy bill in Great Britain predicted to rise to £2,166 The energy price cap in Great Britain will go up by 26% in January to the equivalent of £2,166 a year. However, your bills might not have to rise by the same amount. If you are paying a tariff that matches the price cap you could save by switching to something lower. And if you do it now, you could make a substantial saving. On Wednesday, the cheapest fixed tariff on the market, an 18-month fix from Fuse Energy, was priced at £1,754 for an average home – £412 below the new January cap. It’s worth noting that it’s the price of the energy you use that is fixed, not your bill – so you will still be charged according to what you use. Continue reading...
